newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Motorola sees Q3 below Q2.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Motorola sees Q3 below Q2.

text.p: Motorola Inc said its third quarter earnings may be significantly below its second quarter level and analysts' current expectations for Q3. The company cited continuing weakness in pricing and unit demand in the semiconductor products sector.
Motorola earned $0.54 per share for the second quarter. First Call analysts' mean estimate is $0.50 per share for Q3.
A full text of the company's statement follows.
Motorola expects further pressure on third-quarter results

SCHAUMBURG, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 11, 1996-- Motorola, Inc. said today that sales and order patterns in July and August indicate that earnings for the third quarter ending Sept. 28 may be significantly below those of the second quarter of 1996, as well as significantly below the current expectations of financial analysts in the investment community.

The most significant factor vis-a-vis the second quarter is continuing weakness in pricing and unit demand in the Semiconductor Products Sector, as the semiconductor industry down cycle continues. The company expects the third quarter of 1996 to be the third consecutive quarter in which the industry-wide semiconductor book-to-bill ratio will be less than one. In addition to a continuation of the pricing pressures reported in the second quarter in the cellular telephone, paging and modem businesses, sales and orders thus far in the third quarter have been weaker in international markets. This is affecting the paging and cellular telephone businesses and related component products, such as rechargeable batteries, the company said.
Motorola expects to report its third-quarter results on Oct. 7. Earnings in the second quarter of 1996 were $326 million, or 54 cents per share, on sales of $6.83 billion.

Gary Tooker, vice chairman and chief executive officer, said the factors noted in earlier quarters continue to affect Motorola's financial performance. "Many of our businesses have implemented actions to reduce operating expenses, including hiring restrictions and reductions in work schedules and manufacturing run rates, while attempting to minimize the impact on our employees. We also have deferred capital expenditures, especially in the Semiconductor Products Sector. At the same time, we continue to invest in programs that are critical to our long-term future," he said. "Despite the current difficult conditions in some of our major businesses, we remain confident that the global opportunities for our communications and semiconductor products remain as exciting as ever." -0-

The statements in this press release are forward looking. Pricing pressures and weakening demand in semiconductors, competitive pricing in the paging and cellular telephone businesses, weakness in demand for products, particularly in international markets, the costs associated with introducing a number of new products and the factors listed on pages 11 and 12 of Motorola's Form 10-Q for the period ended June 29, 1996, on pages F-10 and F-11 of Motorola's 1996 proxy statement appendix and in other SEC filings could cause Motorola's actual results to differ materially from those statements. -0-
